findings.title: The test does not check that the hook was refused with closed_error
findings.claim: The test does not check that the hook was refused with closed_error. A ready future from the hook passes just as well as the expected exception.

findings.title: Cleanup is skipped if anything throws between sink
findings.claim: Cleanup is skipped if anything throws between sink.close() and release_close.set_value(). That includes the hook failing with anything other than closed_error, such as stream_closed or broken_promise. In that case the parked close is never released, sink_closed and server_done are never awaited, and the unclosed sink is destroyed.

findings.title: The test waits without a bound on close_entered_cv and then on sink_closed and server_done
findings.claim: The test waits without a bound on close_entered_cv and then on sink_closed and server_done. It relies only on the external harness timeout.

findings.title: The test assumes the stream connection's hook is exactly the second one negotiated and…
findings.claim: The test assumes the stream connection's hook is exactly the second one negotiated and keeps a reference into a growable std::vector.

findings.title: The new test covers only one close order: a client-side stream connection where the sink…
findings.claim: The new test covers only one close order: a client-side stream connection where the sink closes last. It does not cover a source-read-last close (close_source() → stream_close()) or a server-side stream connection, even though both reach the changed stream_close() and send() paths.

findings.title: The new doc says the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed
findings.claim: The new doc says the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed. The corrected sentence a few lines above says closing the client aborts any open stream, and the code does shut stream connections down without both halves closed: through client::abort_all_streams(), server::connection::abort_all_streams(), and the stream loop's own stop_send_loop() on socket error.

findings.title: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from…
findings.claim: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on ... stop_send_loop() waits for _sink_closed_future'. In fact stop_send_loop() when_all's on both `_outgoing_queue_ready` and `_sink_closed_future`. After the std::exchange it simply waits on the substituted ready future.

findings.title: The new comment in stream_close() says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready…
findings.claim: The new comment in stream_close() says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready after the exchange, but stop_send_loop() still moves and waits on _outgoing_queue_ready. Its drain comment also still describes that future as the one that reflects queue drain, which is no longer true once stream_close() has swapped in a ready future.

findings.title: The long explanatory block above the test repeats the root-cause narrative already in…
findings.claim: The long explanatory block above the test repeats the root-cause narrative already in the fix commit message and in the new stream_close() comment, in near-identical wording.

findings.title: The test's header comment, added with the fix, describes the pre-fix behaviour in the…
findings.claim: The test's header comment, added with the fix, describes the pre-fix behaviour in the present tense ('connection::send() still accepts frames', 'the one caller that is not guarded ... is the compressor's send_empty_frame hook'). It also largely repeats the f545c28a commit message.

findings.title: _stream_closing is a second 'refuse to send' flag next to _error, and the guards that…
findings.claim: _stream_closing is a second 'refuse to send' flag next to _error, and the guards that use them have drifted apart. send() checks both flags. enqueue_zero_frame, documented as the 'enlightened copy of connection::send()', checks only _error. stream_close(), and sink_impl::send_buffer()/close() through error(), check only _error. The public error() accessor ignores _stream_closing.

findings.title: stream_close() overwrites `_outgoing_queue_ready` with a ready future
findings.claim: stream_close() overwrites `_outgoing_queue_ready` with a ready future. That breaks send()'s invariant that this future always tracks the tail of `_outgoing_queue`. It is only safe because a guard in a different function (send()) refuses new frames.

findings.title: The new comment says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready after this point
findings.claim: The new comment says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready after this point. That only holds while every other producer is refused. client::enqueue_zero_frame() chains onto _outgoing_queue_ready too, and it checks only _error, not _stream_closing.

findings.title: The test grabs a reference into a growable std::vector (`auto& stream_send_empty_frame =…
findings.claim: The test grabs a reference into a growable std::vector (`auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory.hooks.back();`) and later calls through it. Meanwhile every new client negotiation push_back()s into that same vector.

findings.title: hook_capturing_compressor_factory mutates state from a const negotiate() through…
findings.claim: hook_capturing_compressor_factory mutates state from a const negotiate() through const_cast. The existing cfactory in the same file uses a `mutable` member for the same purpose.

findings.title: The new pass-through compressor copies the existing test_compressor_empty_frames…
findings.claim: The new pass-through compressor copies the existing test_compressor_empty_frames compressor almost exactly: an lz4_fragmented_compressor delegate, the same `data.size ? std::move(data) : rpc::snd_buf(temporary_buffer<char>())` idiom, and the same `negotiate(sstring,bool) { abort(); }` stub.

findings.title: The new compressor fixture is a copy of test_compressor_empty_frames' factory and…
findings.claim: The new compressor fixture is a copy of test_compressor_empty_frames' factory and compressor: the same lz4_fragmented_compressor delegate, the same `data.size ? std::move(data) : rpc::snd_buf(temporary_buffer<char>())` idiom, and the same abort() legacy negotiate overload. Its comment also calls it 'pass-through' although it LZ4-compresses.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl is a middle-man that forwards 15 virtuals to `_inner` by…
findings.claim: test_connected_socket_impl is a middle-man that forwards 15 virtuals to `_inner` by hand, just to swap sink(). test_socket_impl re-creates rpc_socket_impl's shape and ignores the inherited reuseaddr behaviour instead of forwarding it.

findings.title: test_data_sink_impl hard-codes `buffer_size()` to 8192 while forwarding every other…
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl hard-codes `buffer_size()` to 8192 while forwarding every other member to `_inner`. The magic number silently duplicates connected_socket::output()'s default buffer size, which is needed only because the loopback sink has no buffer_size() override.

findings.title: The test names are vague and hide what each piece does
findings.claim: The test names are vague and hide what each piece does. test_sink_state combines parking the close (release_close, close_entered_cv) with recording late puts (put_after_close). test_data_sink_impl, test_connected_socket_impl and test_socket_impl are generic names in a file that already has many socket and sink types.

findings.title: The test's waits have no bound: `close_entered_cv
findings.claim: The test's waits have no bound: `close_entered_cv.wait(...)`, the hook's `.get()`, and `sink_closed.get()`. The fixed loop of 10 yield() calls is described as 'Let the batch flush poller run', which those yields do not guarantee.

findings.title: The documentation says 'Dropping an unclosed sink is an error'
findings.claim: The documentation says 'Dropping an unclosed sink is an error'. In the code, ~sink_impl does SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()), so dropping one aborts the process. The rpc_types.hh doxygen ('close() must be called') also does not mention that this is a fatal assertion.

findings.title: The docs say to 'Read the source until eof or error' and to 'drain what is still in…
findings.claim: The docs say to 'Read the source until eof or error' and to 'drain what is still in flight'. They do not warn that this read can wait forever if the peer never closes its sink, and they give no timeout or abort guidance.

findings.title: The same shutdown contract is written three times: doc/rpc-streaming
findings.claim: The same shutdown contract is written three times: doc/rpc-streaming.md 'Closing a stream', the sink doxygen, and the source doxygen. The new doxygen blocks were also placed above the old '// send data Out...' and '// receive data In...' comments, leaving those old comments between the doxygen and the class.

findings.title: The docs for the send_empty_frame hook on compressor::factory were not updated
findings.claim: The docs for the send_empty_frame hook on compressor::factory were not updated. The commit makes the hook fail with closed_error from the moment stream_close() begins, which is before error() reports anything, yet the factory comment still says nothing about failure.

findings.title: No test covers the second half of the fix, where stream_close() waits for…
findings.claim: No test covers the second half of the fix, where stream_close() waits for _outgoing_queue_ready so that frames accepted before _stream_closing was set are written before write_buf.close(). The new test fires the hook only after close() has already been entered.

findings.title: Only the client-side stream connection is tested
findings.claim: Only the client-side stream connection is tested. The server-side stream connection is a separate entry point with its own negotiate-time hook and teardown, and it is untested.

findings.title: The new doc and API comment say that reading a source until it throws is what closes it
findings.claim: The new doc and API comment say that reading a source until it throws is what closes it. But a throw from unmarshall in process_one_buffer() reaches the caller without close_source() being called. Only failures from stream_receive() close the source.

findings.title: The docs and commit say the connection is shut down only once both halves are closed
findings.claim: The docs and commit say the connection is shut down only once both halves are closed. But _source_closed defaults to true, so on a client sink with no source yet, close() alone runs stream_close().

findings.title: The fix commit lands without its regression test, which arrives in a separate later commit
findings.claim: The fix commit lands without its regression test, which arrives in a separate later commit.

findings.title: stream_close() now waits for every frame already in _outgoing_queue to be written before…
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for every frame already in _outgoing_queue to be written before it closes the write buffer. This wait has no timeout and cannot be cancelled. Before this change, the close went ahead without waiting.

findings.title: The new comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional 'if an entry failed', but a…
findings.claim: The new comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional 'if an entry failed', but a failing send_entry() calls abort() and then p->done.set_value(), so the chain resolves normally. It becomes exceptional only when negotiation fails or stop_send_loop() sets the front entry's done to an exception.

findings.title: The new comment says '_error is only set by the stop() that follows'
findings.claim: The new comment says '_error is only set by the stop() that follows'. _error is also set by abort() when send_entry fails, and that can happen during the new queue_drained wait. stop_send_loop() sets it as well.

findings.title: The test waits without a bound
findings.claim: The test waits without a bound. st.close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout. In addition, any failure between parking the close and st.release_close.set_value(), such as a non-closed_error exception or a failed REQUIRE, leaves the data_sink close parked forever, so sink_closed and the env teardown never complete.

findings.title: The test takes `auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory
findings.claim: The test takes `auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory.hooks.back()`, a reference into a growable std::vector that negotiate() appends to. The stored hooks capture the connection's `this` and outlive their connections, because the factory is declared outside do_with_thread.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl copies the entire connected_socket_impl interface by hand,…
findings.claim: test_connected_socket_impl copies the entire connected_socket_impl interface by hand, but it does not forward the non-pure source(connected_socket_input_stream_config) overload. test_data_sink_impl hard-codes buffer_size() as 8192 instead of forwarding _inner's value.

findings.title: Once _stream_closing is set, send() reports the local stream close to compressor…
findings.claim: Once _stream_closing is set, send() reports the local stream close to compressor send_empty_frame callers as closed_error("connection is closed"), while the socket is still open and _error is false. The sibling sink check for the same sink-closed state reports stream_closed instead. Previously this window returned success, so compressor callers now get a new exceptional result.

findings.title: The PR's validation ran only rpc_test in the debug build, but the contribution guide…
findings.claim: The PR's validation ran only rpc_test in the debug build, but the contribution guide asks for test.py and for tests to pass at least as well as before the patch. The change to send() affects every rpc connection.

findings.title: The new send-admission state is duplicated across _error and _stream_closing, but not…
findings.claim: The new send-admission state is duplicated across _error and _stream_closing, but not all sibling admission checks consult both flags.

findings.title: The regression test does not exercise the queue-drain half of the fix with an entry…
findings.claim: The regression test does not exercise the queue-drain half of the fix with an entry accepted immediately before _stream_closing is set.

findings.title: The new documentation treats any exception from source reading as closing the source,…
findings.claim: The new documentation treats any exception from source reading as closing the source, but deserialization exceptions can escape without invoking close_source().

findings.title: The new queue-drain dependency can make stream_close() wait indefinitely for a queued…
findings.claim: The new queue-drain dependency can make stream_close() wait indefinitely for a queued send blocked by peer backpressure.

findings.title: The comment that _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional 'if an entry failed' gives the…
findings.claim: The comment that _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional 'if an entry failed' gives the wrong source for exceptional completion.

findings.title: The comment says _error is only set by the following stop(), although abort paths can…
findings.claim: The comment says _error is only set by the following stop(), although abort paths can set it while the newly added queue-drain wait is in progress.

findings.title: The changed compressor hook can now fail with closed_error during local stream shutdown,…
findings.claim: The changed compressor hook can now fail with closed_error during local stream shutdown, but the public compressor-factory documentation does not describe this exceptional result.

findings.title: Local stream shutdown is reported to compressor-hook callers as closed_error('connection…
findings.claim: Local stream shutdown is reported to compressor-hook callers as closed_error('connection is closed'), while the sibling sink API represents an already-closed stream with stream_closed.

findings.title: The functional fix and its regression test are split across separate commits even though…
findings.claim: The functional fix and its regression test are split across separate commits even though the PR explicitly recommends cherry-picking the first two commits for backports.

findings.title: The test compressor mutates its hook collection from a const negotiate() using…
findings.claim: The test compressor mutates its hook collection from a const negotiate() using const_cast instead of declaring the test state mutable.

findings.title: The new compressor fixture duplicates the existing empty-frame compressor implementation…
findings.claim: The new compressor fixture duplicates the existing empty-frame compressor implementation and inaccurately describes its LZ4 delegate as pass-through.

findings.title: The socket test double manually forwards most of connected_socket_impl while silently…
findings.claim: The socket test double manually forwards most of connected_socket_impl while silently substituting behavior for members such as reuseaddr and configured input streams.

findings.title: The close-parking and late-put-recording test doubles use generic test_socket/test_sink…
findings.claim: The close-parking and late-put-recording test doubles use generic test_socket/test_sink names that hide their blocking teardown behavior.

findings.title: The shutdown contract is duplicated across the guide and both endpoint API comments,…
findings.claim: The shutdown contract is duplicated across the guide and both endpoint API comments, with no single referenced definition.

findings.title: The stated validation does not satisfy the repository's documented instruction to run test
findings.claim: The stated validation does not satisfy the repository's documented instruction to run test.py.
